chunks: And by this chain, from Al-Hasan ibn Sayf ibn 'Amirah, from Abu Bakr Al-Hadrami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him not fail to recite 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' after the obligatory prayer, for whoever recites it, Allah will gather for him the goodness of this world and the Hereafter, and forgive him and his parents and whatever they beget.

key_terms.خَيْرَ الدُّنْيَا وَ الْآخِرَةِ: The goodness of this world and the Hereafter
key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Say, He is Allah, the One (Surah Al-Ikhlas)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting Surah Al-Ikhlas after obligatory prayers?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the spiritual efficacy of reciting Surah Al-Ikhlas after obligatory prayers, linking it to the accumulation of worldly and otherworldly goodness. It specifically extends the reward of forgiveness to the reciter's parents and their descendants, reflecting the Shia emphasis on familial intercession and the merit of Tawhid in daily worship.
